title: 1975-11-05_SECTION_013_17.txt
concise_summary: This segment serves as the concluding section and afterword to a major block of Exegesis writing (PKD refers to 'these 300,000 words'), in which Dick reformulates his central hermeneutical mistake: he had wrongly accepted linear time as real. He now argues that his 2-3-74 experience was not a Parousia arriving in historical time but rather a personal exaltation into the eternal Platonic world above time, where the visions of Daniel, John of Patmos, and himself are co-present and simultaneous. PKD then develops an intricate theology of the Holy Spirit as a fertilizing, birth-giving entity that implants an incorruptible 'light body' (non-sarx) in the elect — a process he reads through the parables of Jesus, early Christian theoplepsy practices, Orphic mystery religion, and Plato's Timaeus — and concludes that his own experience followed this ancient esoteric protocol, triggered in part by sodium pentothal and the sight of the golden fish ichthys sign.
key_claims: PKD's fundamental error across 300,000 words of Exegesis was accepting the reality of linear time; the Parousia did not arrive in 1974 but exists eternally above time, and PKD was temporarily lifted into that eternal realm.
Daniel, John of Patmos, and PKD all accessed the same eternal, unchanging reality — the world of Platonic forms — not three different historical moments, explaining why their visions correspond.

The Holy Spirit functions as a literal fertilizing agent that implants an incorruptible, non-material 'light body' (non-sarx) in the recipient, constituting a second birth analogous to the virginal conception of Christ by the Holy Spirit.

Jesus communicated the path to the Kingdom of God only to insiders through esoteric parables; this lore was transmitted secretly among early Christians until destroyed by Roman persecution, causing cessation of theoplepsy experiences.

PKD's 2-3-74 experience followed the same causal sequence as ancient mystery religion theoplepsy: prior preparation (votive candle, the golden fish), anamnesis triggered by the ichthys sign (possibly facilitated by sodium pentothal), then theoplepsy.
The Cosmic Christ and the Holy Spirit are closely related or identical — the Holy Spirit is understood as Christ having undergone incarnation and resurrection.
recurring_concepts: Parousia (the saving divine presence, located above rather than at the end of linear time)
Linear time vs. eternal time (the irreality of temporal change; eternity as a realm 'above' history)
Platonic forms (eternal unchanging reality behind the deceptive world of change)
Theoplepsy (divine seizure / possession by the Holy Spirit, compared to Orphic mystery religion)
Anamnesis (Platonic/early Christian recollection; triggered in PKD by the golden fish ichthys sign)
Sarx / non-sarx body (corruptible flesh vs. the incorruptible 'light' or 'ergic' body generated by the Holy Spirit)
The elect / the remnant (those lifted from the 'deluded mass' into vision of eternal reality)
Zoroastrian game-board (cosmic dualism: two antagonists playing out the struggle in linear time)
people_entities: Daniel (Hebrew prophet; PKD places his apocalyptic visions as co-temporal with his own 2-3-74 experience)
John of Patmos (author of Revelation; likewise understood as accessing the same eternal realm as PKD)
Jesus / Christ (divine teacher who encoded the path to the Kingdom in parables for insiders; after resurrection becomes the Cosmic Christ)
John the Baptist (biblical figure; the occasion when the Holy Spirit first descended as a dove upon Jesus)
Mary (mother of Jesus; cited as prototype of Holy Spirit fertilization — the first 'second birth' analogue)
Joseph (father of Jesus; mentioned only to be set aside — Jesus is son of Mary and the Holy Spirit, not Joseph)
Paul / Saint Paul (cited for his teaching that 'flesh cannot inherit the Kingdom of God' and the transformation of sarx)
Plato (philosopher; his Timaeus dialectic of Nous persuading Ananke is PKD's philosophical framework for Grace)
Arachne (mythological figure; her thread used as a maze-navigation metaphor)
texts_works: Book of Daniel (Hebrew Bible; apocalyptic vision text PKD claims to have shared experiential access to)
Revelation / Book of John (New Testament apocalypse; John of Patmos's visions understood as co-present with PKD's)
Acts of the Apostles (New Testament; cited for the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the disciples after Jesus's death)
The Gospels (New Testament; Jesus's parables interpreted esoterically as instructions for attaining the Kingdom)
Timaeus (Plato; the dialectic of Nous and Ananke used to explain how Grace overrides blind efficient causation)
Encyclopedia of Philosophy (unnamed; cited briefly for the proposition 'change is real')
VALIS / 'V A' (PKD's own novel, referenced for its parables of treasure buried in a field as Holy Spirit implantation imagery)
autobiographical: PKD's March 1974 (2-3-74) experience: he describes being 'lifted out of linear time' to perceive the eternal Parousia, which he now reinterprets not as a historical event arriving in 1974 but as personal exaltation into an eternal realm.

The golden fish / ichthys sign: PKD states he was shown a golden fish that caused anamnesis — a sudden flash of recollection — which he now believes was a necessary preparatory step before the theoplepsy.

Sodium pentothal: PKD reports he had recently been given sodium pentothal, and speculates it served a function analogous to a trance-inducing substance in ancient mystery rites, enabling the anamnesis.
Votive candle: PKD mentions lighting a votive candle as one of several preparatory ritual acts performed before his 2-3-74 experience.
Hearing bells: PKD notes he heard bells as part of his experience, associating this with early Christian sacramental anamnesis.
Rome vision: PKD reports having seen Rome and believed in his anamnesis experience prior to the theoplepsy event itself.
The 300,000 words of Exegesis: PKD explicitly characterizes this segment as an afterword and conclusion to a massive body of prior Exegesis writing, acknowledging his central error throughout.
theological_motifs: Parousia (the divine presence or Second Coming, reinterpreted as eternally present above linear time)
Second birth / born from above (Johannine concept of spiritual rebirth; PKD reads it literally as implantation of a non-sarx body by the Holy Spirit)
Adoptionism (Christological position that the Holy Spirit adopted Jesus at baptism rather than at conception)
Paraclete / Second Comforter (the Holy Spirit as promised ongoing divine presence after Christ's departure)
Theoplepsy (divine seizure or possession; PKD's term for the moment the Holy Spirit takes hold of a person)
Anamnesis (Platonic recollection used in early Christian sacramental context; flash of pre-temporal memory)
Sarx / incorruptible body (Pauline distinction between corruptible flesh and the resurrection body; PKD treats the Holy Spirit as generating the latter in the living believer)
Apocalypse as eternal reality (vision of the apocalypse is not a future event but a perception of true eternal reality behind temporal appearances)
Cosmic Christ (the resurrected Christ understood as a cosmic, non-historical entity closely identified with the Holy Spirit)
Holy Wisdom / Sophia (mentioned as one of the eternal living forms; aligned with the Holy Spirit's guidance)
Nous / Ananke dialectic (Plato's Timaeus: divine Reason persuading material Necessity; mapped onto Grace vs. blind causation)
Selection / Judgment (the purpose of the veiled linear-time world is a process of growth and selection among souls)
The elect / remnant (those who make the correct choice and are elevated from the deluded mass)
literary_self_ref: PKD cites 'V A' (VALIS) explicitly as a novel containing the parable of the treasure buried in the field, the mustard seed, and related seed/grain imagery, interpreting these as encodings of the Holy Spirit's fertilizing function — suggesting his fiction was unconsciously or deliberately transmitting the esoteric theological lore he is now decoding.

The phrase 'as in V A, my novel' directly identifies the treasure/seed parables in VALIS as parallel to the Gospel parables about the Kingdom of God, collapsing the boundary between PKD's fiction and canonical scripture.
symbols_images: The game-board (Zoroastrian cosmological image: the world as a playing surface where Light and Darkness compete across linear time)
The veil (linear time as a veil concealing eternal reality, necessary for the process of judgment/selection to function)
Arachne's thread through the maze (guidance metaphor: the Christian must follow a thread to navigate the deceptive labyrinth of existence)
Seed / grain buried in rich soil (Holy Spirit as fertilizing agent implanted in the receptacle of the human person)
The mustard seed (starts astonishingly small; figures the implanted spiritual element that grows to transform the whole being)
Yeast that leavens the whole mass (Holy Spirit gradually transforming the entire person from within)
Pearl of great price (the implanted spiritual treasure, recognized only by those who seek it)
The golden fish / ichthys (early Christian symbol; the specific object that triggered PKD's anamnesis in 3-74)
The dove descending at baptism (symbol of the Holy Spirit's first advent to Jesus; type of the adoptionist moment)
Egg / seed / treasure / grain / pearl (cluster of synonymous images for the Holy Spirit's implant in the human receptacle)
Lambs vs. goats (Gospel parable figure; lambs as the elect who can hear the good shepherd's voice)
The harvest (Christ as cosmic harvester gathering those he has planted; figures corporate afterlife with the Cosmic Christ)
Child's play store (metaphor for the reduced, illusory quality of temporal reality during the period of choosing)
tensions: PKD asserts this segment is a conclusive 'afterword' resolving his prior 300,000-word error, yet the text itself continues to speculate and hedge ('I think anyhow,' 'if I am right'), suggesting the resolution is provisional rather than final.

PKD claims his 2-3-74 experience was a lifting out of linear time into eternal reality, but simultaneously constructs a sequential causal narrative (sodium pentothal → anamnesis → theoplepsy) that is itself thoroughly linear and temporal.

He adopts an adoptionist Christology (the Holy Spirit came to Jesus at baptism) while also asserting the virginal conception (Christ is son of Mary and the Holy Spirit, not Joseph) — these are competing, historically antagonistic Christological positions that he does not reconcile.

PKD argues that the esoteric Christian lore enabling theoplepsy was destroyed by Roman persecution and thus lost, yet he himself apparently underwent the same process without access to the lore — raising the question of how his preparatory acts (votive candle, the fish) were performed correctly.

The Holy Spirit is described as both 'moving backward, secretly, from the conclusion of time' (retrocausal/eschatological agency) and as a present fertilizing entity generating a 'light body' in the living believer — temporal directions of the Spirit's action are conflated.
PKD equates the Cosmic Christ with the Holy Spirit yet also treats them as sequentially distinct (the Holy Spirit comes after Christ withdraws), without resolving this conflation.
evidence_quotes: "What I have been drawn more L more to in my exegesis is the realization that linear time is somehow not real; which is to say, the changes in it (time as a reality is debatable, but as the k? encyclopedia of philosophy says, 'change is real') are somehow not real. I am not back in Biblical times, but somehow John & Daniel & I found ourselves in the same reality or time frame, an eternal unchanging world above & beyond time. It is real, and the changing world within time is not."

"My whole basic mistake in all these 300,000 words has been to accept on face value the reality of linear time and the changes therein. The Parousia did not set in on linear time in 74; I was lifted up out of linear time, to see the Parousia which is always there."

"The Holy Spirit is birth-giving; in the Bible it impregnates Mary, so she 'is with child,' Jesus, or else it adopts him; in any case later on when it comes to a person one speaks of a second birth, not from the womb, but of water and spirit, a birth from above."

"I would say in conclusion: 'We are here to choose the true from the counterfeit, and we will be given much time, perhaps thousands of years, and when and if we do chose correctly at last, we will then be shown what we have chosen: shown what reality is like. And not before; for during the chosing all is reduced, as in a child's play store.'"
"It was moving backward, secretly, from the conclusion of time, and so knew in advance what was going to happen."
uncertainty_flags: The text reference 'V A, my novel' appears to indicate VALIS, but VALIS was not published until 1981; in 1975 PKD may be referring to an early draft or manuscript under a working title — the precise work intended should be verified against manuscript records.

PKD's claim that early Christian theoplepsy lore was 'lost when they were killed by the Romans' is a historical assertion with no citation and is not consistent with standard early church historiography; a scholar should note this as PKD's private historical construction.

The 'k? encyclopedia of philosophy' reference is garbled (likely 'the encyclopedia of philosophy' but the letter/abbreviation is unclear in transcription); the specific edition and entry PKD is citing cannot be confirmed.

PKD mentions sodium pentothal in connection with his 3-74 period — it is unclear from this passage whether he received it medically (e.g., as an anesthetic) or in another context; the biographical circumstances should be verified.

PKD treats adoptionism and virginal conception as compatible Christological positions within a single paragraph, but these were historically mutually exclusive positions in early Christianity; his synthesis here is theologically idiosyncratic and may reflect confusion rather than deliberate syncretism.

The reference to 'Arachne's thread' is unusual — Ariadne's thread is the canonical maze-navigation myth; Arachne is the weaver transformed into a spider. PKD may be conflating the two mythological figures, or this may be a transcription error.
reading_excerpt: I am not back in Biblical times, but somehow John & Daniel & I found ourselves in the same reality or time frame, an eternal unchanging world above & beyond time. It is real, and the changing world within time is not.
raw_text: always defeated. The elect are, were and will always be saved (thus I remembed back thousands of years). Eternity does not lie at the end of linear time but above it; the saving presence (the Parousia) lies above, not at the end, although when linear time ends it probably collapses back into eternity, so that is nominally true. My whole basic mistake in all these 300,000 words has been to accept on face value the reality of linear time and the changes therein. The Parousia did not set in on linear time in 74; I was lifted up out of linear time, to see the Parousia which is always there. Thus it did come — for me, in this manner: ray reward, so to speak, as I was exalted up from the "deluded mass" into the "remnant." (I think anyhow.) I saw what Daniel & John saw because that is how it is in the eternal world of Platonic forms; that is what is, and it was then when they saw it. Thus I adopt the Zoroastrian "game-board" view of this world, as a place where the two antagonists play it out through hand after hand in linear time. My task has been to explain (1) How the Parousia came and did not come; (2) How everything, in 74, happened and did not happen — at the same time. In think now I have done this. --- END --- -1- AFTERWORD What I have been drawn more L more to in my exegesis is the realization that linear time is somehow not real; which is to say, the changes in it (time as a reality is debatable, but as the k? encyclopedia of philosophy says, "change is real") are somehow not real. I am not back in Biblical times, but somehow John & Daniel & I found ourselves in the same reality or time frame, an eternal unchanging world above & beyond time. It is real, and the changing world within time is not. Without accepting this it is impossible to explain my experience and theirs. For, Where were we? and, What did we see? Another world. And certain things are always there, and certain events are always happening. It was true in Daniel's time, in John's and mine. What is real is the Apocalypse. Or, put better, what we call a "vision of the apocalypse" is in fact a vision of authentic eternal true reality lying behind the deceptive linear-time world of change. Inescapably, as I tried to account for my experience, I have been led to realize the irreality of linear time & the changes therein. What I did was I got outside time in 3-74. Kb More ac¬ curately, I was lifted out of, by another mind. I am now back in it, like everyone else; but I saw what I saw. I would say that our linear time world is framed for us, veiled, so that we may perform under the scrutiny of selection (judgment). The veil serves a valid purpose, and is not lifted until after judgment, at which time the game is over, and the veil not necessary; as a piece we have been lifted from the board forever. Although we remain unaware of supernatural entities they guide and direct us. I assume us to be in a growth process the final end of which is invisible to us. Selection as to who grew, who didn't and in what way is not ours but theirs. Since Daniel wrote before Christ, I assume this eternal world existed then, and Christ came from it to acquaint us with it. It was his purpose to give men the clues, to unravel the riddles of existence so that they could surmount the linear-time world and enter the Kingdom. Without Christ and his clues, no one could or would ever unravel the riddles, so it was not until the First Advent that men began entering the Kingdom. He then withdrew, like his father the steersman, to a detached point, and gathered (s) up the harvest he planted; i.e. those who act rightly. (Follow the thread, like Arachne's thread, through the maze we are in.) (The main riddle is to locate the side of Light in its struggle against Darkness, to join it and act for it.) (It is here but hidden, as is the darkness; they are not evident or evidently unmixed, and choice is difficult.) (Intent is a good first step, as in it is contained basic knowledge —assessment— of the situation.) (In a very true way it can be said we have been placed arbitrarily away from home and must find our way back; that is the goal.) I would say in conclusion: "We are here to choose the true from the counterfeit, and we will be given much time, perhaps thousands of years, and when and if we do chose correctly at last, we will then be shown what we have chosen: shown what reality is like. And not before; for during the chosing all is reduced, as in a child's play store." -2- We live as children and choose as children, but once we choose correctly we become true adults. Only then does the real purpose of life become evident; before that it was a dream and a guess and a search among mists. Only the forms are real; and they are alive...such as Holy Wisdom. Holy Spirit — born from above — adoptionist view (of Christ: the dove descending at baptism) — fertilization. The superior life fcrm parent was present, then left. The seed/egg/treasure/grain/ pearl remains, to hatch upon death of body. I.e. upon falling away of corruptible body (sarx). Christ was the first one the spirit came to, when John the Baptist was baptising him; then after Jesus' death the Holy Spirit (the "second comforter" or Paraclete) came to the others. And created immortal incorruptible bodies in them, too, such as Christ had (obtained). This is what happened to me in 3-74. The incorruptible body is the offspring, so to speak, of the parent, the Holy Spirit; it gives birth to it, the second birth or being "born from above," born of spirit and water, not from the womb; without you do that you cannot inherit the Kingdom of God. My experience is connected with the promise that the Holy Spirit (or Christ) would come and speak when one was hauled before the magistrate, but I think it/she quickened while here, as well. It was moving backward, secretly, from the conclusion of time, and so knew in advance what was going to happen. The Holy Spirit is birth¬ giving; in the Bible it impregnates Mary, so she "is with child," Jesus, or else it adopts him; in any case later on when it comes to a person one speaks of a second birth, not from the womb, but of water and spirit, a birth from above. This is amazingly con¬ sistent: Christ is not the son of Mary and Joseph, but the son of Mary and the Holy Spirit. The disciples, born of human parents, were born again in a manner resembling the way Jesus was originally born; they became the progeny of the Holy Spirit, perhaps more literally than we think, in this second birth, from above. It is important that Jesus says that ONLY by this second birth, ffom above, that a manz can inherit the Kingdom of God; therefore this must produce the nonsarx body, as when it is said, "Flesh cannot inherit the Kingdom of God," and Paul speaks of the flesh, sarx, changing into something else. I have a feeling that receiving the Holy Spirit produces an actual second birth, and starts a process by which a second incorruptible nonmaterial body, such as that which Christ had after the resurrection comes into being, a "light" or ergic body; as in mentioned in V A, my novel, the many parables about the treasure buried in the field, the seed, the grain, plus that about the pearl, all refer to the impregnation or fertilization or implantation or anyhow the quickening achieved by the Hoiv Spirit upon the person it comes to. Clearest is the "yeast which leavens the whole mass," which when considered with the treasure, the mustard seed, the seeds, the solitary grain "buried in rich soil" — as in V A, they suggest something valuable placed in a recptacle, and, as with the yeast, it changes the receptacle. "Leavening" it throughout, eventually. The mustard seed one suggests it starts out astonishingly small. Remember, at the time Jesus told these parables, the Paraclete hadn't come to the disciples to achieve this with them; Jesus was preparing them for this event, which came *had to come* after he himself lost his sarx and acquired his resurrected body. Yes, the parables prepared them for what was to come, as in ACTS. In the gospels they do not yet understand. Also in the parables, such as the goats-lambs one, he suggests those who are the lambs, or are his crop, are called by him or harvested by him; they join him, in what I construe to be a corporate life beyond the grave. "Lambs" are a good symbol because lambs can hear the good shepherd, whereas treasures and pearls and seeds can't; at the very most grain or seeds sprouted can be harvested. They, who are twice born, wind up with him, obviously meaning the Cosmic Christ who I think is closely related to if not identical witn (at least in certain ways) to the Holy Spirit. I say, it is the Holy Spirit having gone through incarnation and being resurrected. * * The manifestation of the Holy Spirit to rescue me (God's Grace) conforms exactly to Plato's concept of Noos "persuading" ananke along the lines of wisdom; i.e. the inter¬ play between efficient causes —which would have led to my doom— and final causes, Holy Wisdom, follow Plato's schema precisely: I felt Wisdom take over control and direction. The dialectic which is described in Timeus. A situation of blind decay was leading into a cul de sac. Yet — I performed the early Xtian sacraments, and experienced the Xtian anamnesis, so it was the Holy Spirit; and I heard the bells. In the parables Jesus taught his disciples how to attain the Kingdom of God; he didn't want outsiders to know. Integral in this is receiving the Holy Spirit — I adjudge this to be the x prime event in it all. So evidently certain things, secret preparatory things, must be done in order that —if I am right— the Holy Spirit will come. I think I am right. This lore, this esoteric knowledge, was passed on by Christian to Christian; through it, spec, the practice of it, their obtained the theolepsy. But the lore was lost, when they were killed by the Romans. Thus people ceased to attain the Kingdom, because, I think, they did not know and perform what was needed. Well, the Holy Spirit came to me, but I think I had to do many things in preparation; I have been certain of it, without relating this to the parables or early Christianity. The votive candle, and I had to be shown the golden fish; there must have been others. The fish, right then and there, caused anamnesis. Doesn't this sound like the Orphic and perhaps other theolepsy mystery religions? I saw Rome and believed in my anamnesis experience before the spirit came; of everything I think the golden-fish-induced anamnesis made the thaiepsy possible. And I think anamnesis wouldn't have occured if I hadn't just been given the sodium penthathol, which probably served to replace some trance¬ like state of the mysteries. Something known to Christianity, a state very altered. There was some ancient equivilent, perhaps even drug induced.
